questions.stem: A patient was given an antimicrobial for diabetic gastroparesis as an off-label indication. Which of the following antibiotics act on motilin receptors and increase GI motility?
questions.solutionHtml:
Erythromycin

Motilin:

  • Endogenous peptide produced mainly in the duodenum
  • Endogenous motilin is responsible for the initiation of phase iii contractions of the migrating motor complex(MMC)
  • MMC helps in clearing the stomach and intestine of luminal secretions, undigested material, and bacteria during the inter digestive period
  • Administration of exogenous drugs that stimulate motilin receptors accelerate gastric emptying
  • Example
  • Macrolides: azithromycin, erythromycin, Clarithromycin


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 12th Edition, Page Number: 1327

questions.stem: Which of the following is a stool softener?
questions.solutionHtml:
Docussates
  • Docusate salts
  • Are anionic surfactants/ stool wetting agents
  • Softens the stools by net water accumulation in the lumen
  • Lower the surface tension of the stool to allow mixing of aqueous and fatty substances, softening the stool and permitting easier defecation
  • These agents also stimulate intestinal fluid and electrolyte secretion (possibly by increasing mucosal cyclic amp) and alter intestinal mucosal permeability
  • Docusate sodium and docusate calcium are available in several dosage forms.

Lactulose

Is an osmotic purgative

Bisacodyl

Is a stimulant laxative

Bran

Is a bulk-forming laxative



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 723

questions.stem: Among all the laxatives, we use Lactulose in hepatic encephalopathy. All are reasons for its usage in hepatic encephalopathy except:

options.label: A
options.text: Lactulose causes a reduction of blood ammonia concentration by 25-50 percent

options.label: B
options.text: The breakdown products of lactulose are alkaline

options.label: C
options.text: Ammonia produced by bacteria in the colon is converted to ionized ammonium salts

options.label: D
options.text: Ionized ammonium salts that are formed are not absorbed from the intestine

questions.answerText: The breakdown products of lactulose are alkaline
questions.solutionHtml:
The breakdown products of lactulose are alkaline

USE of Lactulose in hepatic encephalopathy:

  • Lactulose causes reduction of blood nh3 concentration by 25-50 percent
  • Breakdown products of lactulose are acidic
  • Acidic ph lowers the ph of stools
  • Ammonia produced by bacteria in the colon is converted to ionized nh4+ salts that are not absorbed


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 725

questions.stemHtml: A gastroenterologist identified on colonoscopy, there is a discoloration of the membranes lining the large intestine and rectum resulting from the deposit of pigment in the lamina propria. The patient had no other symptoms and the doctor asked him drug history. The long-term usage of one of the laxatives is known to cause adverse effects as shown in the Image?
questions.solutionHtml:
Senna
  • Melanosis coli is an adverse effect of anthraquinone laxatives like senna, cascara sagrada
  • Melanotic pigmentation of the colonic mucosa is called melanosis coli
  • seen in patients taking anthraquinone laxatives for long at least 4-9 months
  • Histologically, this is caused by the presence of pigment-laden macrophages within the lamina propria
  • The condition is benign and reversible on discontinuation of the laxative
  • These agents also have been associated with the development of "cathartic colon,"

Note:

  • Liquid paraffin is known to cause foreign body granuloma


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 724

questions.stem: Prucalopride is used in women with chronic constipation in whom laxatives fail to provide adequate relief. The drug acts by?
questions.solutionHtml:
5HT 4 Agonist

Prucalopride:

  • Is a specific 5ht4 receptor agonist
  • Facilitates cholinergic neurotransmission
  • Acts throughout the length of the intestine, increasing oral-cecal transit and colonic transit without affecting gastric emptying
  • Approved or use in women with chronic constipation in whom laxatives fail to provide adequate relief


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 924

questions.stem: Which of the following is an incorrect statement regarding H2 blockers?

options.label: A
options.text: They block H2 receptors reversibly competing with histamine for binding

options.label: B
options.text: They predominantly inhibit stimulated acid secretion

options.label: C
options.text: They help in duodenal ulcer healing because they suppress nocturnal acid secretion

options.label: D
options.text: H2 blockers are dosed in the night

questions.answerText: They predominantly inhibit stimulated acid secretion
questions.solutionHtml:
They predominantly inhibit stimulated acid secretion
  • H2 receptors are present on the basolateral membrane of parietal cells
  • They block H2 receptors reversibly competing with histamine for binding but PPIs Block H+/K+ ATPase enzyme irreversibly
  • Predominantly inhibit basal acid secretion compared to stimulated acid secretion
  • Inhibit basal acid secretion helps in duodenal ulcer healing because they suppress nocturnal acid secretion
  • So H2 blockers are dosed in the night


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 697

questions.stem: Following are the drugs used for IBS-constipation predominant except
questions.solutionHtml:
Alosetron

Alosetron is used to treat women with severe irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) who have diarrhea as the main problem. It is not a cure, but it may help to decrease abdominal pain, sudden urges to have a bowel movement, and diarrhea

questions.stem: A 74-year-old patient suffering from chronic constipation complained of very loose stools after treatment with bisacodyl, one tablet daily for 1 week. Which of the following would be the best advice to give to this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: There is no cause for alarm, the situation is self-limiting.

options.label: B
options.text: Continue bisacodyl, but take the medication with a small snack.

options.label: D
options.text: Discontinue bisacodyl, and increase fiber and fluid intake.

questions.answerText: Discontinue bisacodyl, and increase fiber and fluid intake.
questions.solutionHtml:
Discontinue bisacodyl, and increase fiber and fluid intake.
  • Reason- When diarrhea is experienced with the use of laxatives, the laxative should be discontinued until the resolution of diarrhea.
  • A diet rich in fiber and abundant fluid intake usually helps to normalize the intestine.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:- 723-724

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with terminal metastatic lung cancer had been hospitalized for 3 months. His renal function had deteriorated, and laboratory results showed serum creatinine 4.5 m g/dL (normal 0.9−1.2 m g/dL) and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) 75 m g/dL (normal 6−20 m g/dL). Because of poor food intake, immobility, and the requirement for opioid analgesia, the patient was severely constipated and required daily laxative therapy. Which of the following would be a suitable laxative for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lactulose

Reason- Lactulose is a nonabsorbable sugar that is hydrolyzed in the colon to organic acids. These acids draw water into the lumen by osmotic forces, stimulating colonic propulsive motility by stretching the colonic wall. The laxative effect is mild.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:- 724

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman presents to the clinic for a follow-up of her abdominal pain. The pain has been occurring for a couple of years but has worsened recently. She is often constipated and then will have periods of diarrhea. Her pain does usually improve after a bowel movement. After multiple negative tests, the diagnosis of constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome is made. Which of the following is an appropriate treatment for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tegaserod

Reason- Tegaserod is a 5-HT4 serotonin receptor agonist used in the treatment of constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome. The 5-HT4 receptor is thought to help control GI motility; therefore, being an agonist will increase GI motility and prevent constipation.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:- 724

questions.stem: A 58-year-old alcoholic man suffering from hepatic cirrhosis was admitted to the hospital because of drowsiness and disorientation in time and place. Further exams led to the diagnosis of portal-systemic encephalopathy. Which of the following drugs would be appropriate to eliminate toxic enteric products in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lactulose
  • Reason-Eliminating toxic enteric products (mainly fecal ammonia) is a therapeutic goal in portal-systemic encephalopathy. Patients with severe liver disease have an impaired capacity to detoxify ammonia coming from the colon, where it is produced by bacterial metabolism of fecal urea.
  • Ammonia is an important cause of brain toxicity. Lactulose, in high doses, can lower colonic pH, which results in the “trapping” of the ammonia by its conversion to polar ammonium ion, which is poorly absorbed.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:- 724

questions.stem: A 53-year-old woman complained to her physician that the drug she was taking did not work and that she was still suffering from obstinate constipation. The woman had a long history of irritable bowel syndrome and took several drugs in the past with limited success. She was presently taking lactulose. The physician decided to try another drug recently approved for irritable bowel syndrome with constipation in adult women. The drug is a proteinoid derivative that acts by opening type 2 chloride channels in the small intestine. Which of the following drugs was most likely prescribed?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lubiprostone

  • Reason- Lubiprostone is a prokinetic drug that acts in the small intestine. Several agents, commonly called laxatives, can stimulate intestinal motility in nonspecific or indirect ways, but the term prokinetic generally is reserved for agents that enhance intestinal transit through interaction with specific receptors. Lubiprostone is a prostaglandin E1 derivative that appears to bind to prostaglandin E4 receptors linked to the activation of adenylyl cyclase. This in turn can open specific type 2 chloride channels in the luminal cells of the intestinal epithelium, increasing chloride-rich fluid secretion into the intestine. Clinically, lubiprostone alters stool consistency and promotes regular bowel movements. Signs and symptoms related to constipation, including abdominal bloating, abdominal discomfort, stool consistency, and straining, are improved, and long-term data suggest a sustained response over a 6- to 12-month treatment period.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:- 724
